subject: Re: Follow-up: Private VPC networking options / next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@fintechco.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Private VPC networking options / next steps

Hi Sarah and Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we stay aligned: 

Summary of call:
- FinTechCo is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing inference workloads (low-latency payments risk scoring) and wants isolation and direct networking between their AWS VPC and our Private control plane.
- Primary concerns: data egress controls, connection stability, support for high-throughput bursts, and ability to host the KV cache locally.

Options we covered (short):
1) Hosted API (no VPC): fastest to get started, but traffic routes over the public internet — not acceptable for this use case.
2) Dedicated capacity: single-tenant inference capacity on our infra, can be combined with IP allowlists for control plane access; still routes control-plane traffic over public endpoints unless you request PrivateLink.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): full VPC-hosted control plane, supports AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering; recommended for regulated workloads.

Technical notes specific to FinTechCo:
- You expressed preference for PrivateLink over VPC peering because of cross-account simplicity and to avoid route table changes.
- You need a static set of egress IPs for allowlisting in downstream systems (payments gateways).
- Compliance will want KMS key policy alignment and audit log forwarding.

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa: share the network requirements doc and a single-page diagram showing PrivateLink + allowed egress flows (attached).
- FinTechCo: confirm whether you prefer AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering for control plane and whether you can accept our recommended NAT egress config.
- Schedule a network readiness call next week (30-45 min) to walk through VPC endpoints, SGs, and routing.

If this recap looks right, can you confirm ownership for network engineering on your side and a preferred time window for the call?

Thanks,
Sean
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: redwood-private-vpc-network-diagram.pdf (1 page stub)
Attachment: network-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@fintechco.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private VPC networking options / next steps

Hi Sean — thanks for the recap. This looks accurate. A couple of clarifying Qs before we confirm the network team and time: 

1) PrivateLink vs VPC peering: we do prefer PrivateLink for the control plane to avoid route table exposures, but curious about limitations — e.g., is there any throughput cap or per-connection cold start latency we should watch for?

2) Egress IPs: we host downstream calls to payment gateways that require IP allowlisting. Can you provide a static egress IP range or do you expect to publish a list (ideally /24-ish)? Any options if we need more deterministic NAT?

3) Audit logs: we need to know whether Redwood can push audit logs to our S3 or whether we'll pull from your audit API. Also need KMS integration details (we will provide a customer-managed KMS key).

I'll loop in our network lead when we confirm — likely Ana Rodriguez (cc'ing when ready). For now, availability for the network call: Wed 2027-03-31 09:00-11:00 PT or Thu 2027-04-01 13:00-15:00 PT.

Thanks,
Sarah
Head of Infrastructure | FinTechCo
sarah.jenkins@fintechco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@fintechco.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@fintechco.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private VPC networking options / next steps

Hi Sarah — great questions, answered inline below. I'll plan to walk these in the network call as well and can share expanded docs if helpful.

1) PrivateLink throughput/latency:
- PrivateLink is the recommended pattern for control-plane traffic. For our control plane endpoints (API/management) we see negligible additional latency compared to public endpoints (typical added latency <5ms inside same region).
- Throughput: PrivateLink itself scales with ENIs and we support bursting to handle spikes typical of inference workloads. If you expect sustained extreme throughput, we can provision additional ENIs on the endpoint service side — we can discuss expected RPS during the call and provision ahead of time.

2) Static egress IPs and deterministic NAT options:
- For Private deployments we provide two egress options: (a) customer-managed NAT in your VPC (you control the public IPs), or (b) our managed egress with a published pool of static IPs we can reserve for your tenancy.
- If you require a /24, our managed pool can allocate contiguous IPs where available; otherwise we recommend customer-managed NAT for full control. We'll need to know if downstream partners require a single IP or a range.

3) Audit logs & KMS: 
- Audit logs: we support two patterns: push logs to your S3 bucket via cross-account role, or you can pull from our audit API for a period (we retain logs per the agreement). Push to S3 is the most straightforward for compliance teams.
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS keys (CMKs) for encrypting data at rest. We'll need the ARN and a short key policy allowing our service role to use/decrypt. We can provide a template key policy during the call.

Attachments: I've re-attached the single-page diagram and a short checklist (network-requirements.xlsx) that shows required SGs, endpoints, IP ranges, and IAM role steps.

Proposed updated next steps:
- FinTechCo to confirm preference for egress (managed vs customer NAT) and whether a /24 is required for gateways.
- Ana Rodriguez (network lead) to join the call.
- Schedule: Wed 2027-03-31 09:30 PT — works for our network engineer (Dylan). If that works for you, I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short technical readout and then loop in procurement for contract questions.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0246
